headline: US President Donald Trump denied limiting Ukraine's access to the Starshield military internet network after a speed limit hampered Ukraine's drones, and said he did not think Elon Musk had done so either.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an on-record presidential denial in a live war, but who gave the order is disputed and unproven.
importance_line: A slowdown of the military internet link that Ukraine's drones use matters most to Ukrainian defenders and civilians, who were hit by deadly strikes after the slowdown, and to US lawmakers demanding an inquiry, but who gave the order is still disputed and Trump says he is not sure the service ever went down.
summary: The BBC reports that US President Donald Trump said it was not him and that he did not think it was Elon Musk when asked about a speed limit on Starshield, the military version of Musk's Starlink satellite internet network, which cut off weapons flying faster than 100 mph (160 km/h), adding that he was "not sure" it "ever came down". His denial answers a Reuters report on Thursday 15 Oct, citing two unnamed US officials and one Western official, that the order came from inside the White House, and Musk's own suggestion that the US government may have been behind it, while Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had not been restored.
notes: Reply story: Trump answers Reuters (Thursday 15 Oct) and Musk. The speed limit itself dates from Tuesday 13 Oct 2026; today's news is Trump's denial on Friday 16 Oct. The BBC page uses Starlink and Starshield almost interchangeably; the denial is about Starshield.
